questions.question: What are CrewAI's four primitives?
options: Model, Prompt, Tool, Memory
Agent (role+goal+backstory+tools), Task (unit of work), Crew (container), Process (execution strategy)
Actor, Message, Router, Aggregator
Node, Edge, State, Checkpoint
questions.explanation: CrewAI's four primitives are: Agent (role + goal + backstory + tools), Task (description + expected_output + assigned agent), Crew (container sequencing agents and tasks with a Process), and Process (Sequential, Hierarchical, or Consensual).

questions.question: What is the key difference between CrewAI Crews and Flows?
options: Crews are free, Flows require a paid license
Crews are autonomous LLM-driven collaboration for exploration; Flows are event-driven, code-owned, deterministic workflows for production
Crews support multiple models; Flows only support one
Crews run in parallel; Flows run sequentially
questions.explanation: Crews are autonomous and LLM-driven — good for open-ended tasks like research and brainstorming. Flows are event-driven with code-owned graphs — deterministic, testable, and observable, making them the recommended starting point for production.

questions.question: What does CrewAI's 2026 documentation recommend as the starting point for production applications?
options: Start with Crews for maximum autonomy
Start with a Flow; fold Crews in as sub-steps only when autonomy earns its cost
Start with the Hierarchical process for maximum control
Start with a single Agent and scale up
questions.explanation: CrewAI's 2026 docs explicitly recommend: 'for any production-ready application, start with a Flow.' Crews are for exploration and creative collaboration; Flows are for observable, auditable, production-grade deployments.

questions.question: What are the four built-in memory types CrewAI ships?
options: RAM, disk, cache, archive
Short-term (within run), long-term (across runs), entity (per-entity facts), contextual (retrieval-time assembly)
Episodic, semantic, procedural, working
User, session, agent, global
questions.explanation: CrewAI ships four memory types out of the box: short-term (within the current run), long-term (persists across runs), entity (per-entity facts about customers, accounts, etc.), and contextual (assembled at retrieval time).

questions.question: What is the 'backstory bloat' anti-pattern in CrewAI?
options: Using the same backstory for multiple agents
Writing 2000-word backstories that push out context budget without adding useful guidance
Not writing any backstory at all
Including code examples in the backstory
questions.explanation: Backstory bloat is the anti-pattern of writing very long agent backstories (2000+ words) that push context budget without proportional gains in agent quality. Keep backstories tight — they are tone and judgment shapers, not encyclopedias.

questions.question: When should you use a Hierarchical process in CrewAI?
options: For any task with more than one step
Only when you have 4+ specialist agents where a manager Agent needs to route dynamically
For all production deployments
When task ordering is unknown in advance
questions.explanation: The Hierarchical process adds a manager Agent that routes between specialist agents. Use it only when you have 4+ specialists — adding a manager for fewer agents adds complexity without benefit.
